opfunu_remap.rule: opfunu_class_index(fid) = 1 if fid == 1 else fid - 1 (opfunu's own F<k> class name, e.g. fid=21 -> F20).
opfunu_remap.derivation: opfunu numbers CEC2017 CONTIGUOUSLY (F1..F29, no gap for the withdrawn fid 2 -- opfunu/cec_based/cec2017.py's own class sequence, grepped directly). Its own bias/formula for class Fk matches the DEFINITIONS PDF's Table I row k (the SAME contiguous, no-gap numbering cec2017/mod.rs's own module doc already documents diverges from the code's gapped func_num for the report's own prose) -- so Fk's INTENDED sezgi counterpart is Table row k's real func_num, which is k+1 for k>=2 (the gap at func_num 2 pushes every later slot up by one) and k itself for k=1 (before the gap). Empirically verified, not merely asserted: t8_probe_remap.py evaluated every opfunu class against every sezgi fid at 3 points and confirmed F1 is the ONLY class that numerically agrees with any sezgi fid (fid 1) -- every other class (F2..F29) diverges from ALL 29 sezgi fids at every probed point, consistent with the two independent bug classes documented below (data-source offset for F2-F19, per-component defects for the composition classes F20-F29) that make the 'intended' Table-row correspondence never actually hold numerically.
opfunu_remap.opfunu_f2_status: EXCLUDED entirely, not merely tagged -- per this milestone's own scope ruling (task-8-brief.md item 6): F2 does not correspond to any REAL CEC2017 function (Zakharov formula applied to the withdrawn fid 2's own dead shift/rotation data), so it is skipped as expected-disagreement-by-construction. It is still evaluated and stored in this fixture's fid-3 points (tagged 'opfunu-f2-bogus-withdrawn-data') for transparency, exactly like every other excluded point, rather than omitted from the JSON.

probe_points.o: for fid 1,3-20: the official CEC2017 shift vector, first `dim` values of shift_data_<fid>.txt's single row. For fid 21-30 (composition): component 1's shift row (first `dim` values of shift_data_<fid>.txt's FIRST LINE) -- the same `x = comp_shift[0]` pin cec2017/mod.rs's own T8 module-doc section proves algebraically reduces to F_i* for every composition fid.
probe_points.random: python3 random.Random(20170101 + fid*100 + dim).uniform(-80.0, 80.0) drawn `dim` times -- one independent seeded draw per (fid,dim) combination, fully reproducible (t8_points.py in this task's report). Absolute domain point (not offset from `o`), range [-80,80] comfortably inside the suite's [-100,100] domain -- same numeric range/shape T5's own cec2014 fixture used, base seed swapped to this suite's own report-publication-year-styled 20170101.

header.dims: {10,30} only -- this milestone's vendored scope (cec2017/mod.rs module doc's 'Vendoring scope' section); the C itself also supports {2,20,50,100} but those dims were never vendored.

divergence_classes.opfunu-f2-bogus-withdrawn-data: NEW for CEC2017 (this task's own remap-derivation finding, empirically verified via t8_probe_remap.py). opfunu 1.0.4's CEC2017 numbers the suite CONTIGUOUSLY, no gap at the officially withdrawn fid 2 (opfunu/cec_based/cec2017.py's own F1..F29 class sequence, grepped directly). Its own 'F2' class (F22017), the one whose Table-row position and bias (200.0) correspond to sezgi fid 3 (the REAL Zakharov, F*=300 in the C's own gapped func_num numbering), is constructed `f_shift="shift_data_2", f_matrix="M_2_D"` -- i.e. it reads the C reference's shift_data_2.txt/M_2_D<dim>.txt, which is the OFFICIALLY WITHDRAWN fid 2's own dead data (never vendored into crates/problems/data/cec2017/ at all, per cec2017/mod.rs's own F2 ruling), NOT the real Zakharov's own shift_data_3.txt/M_3_D. Verified: opfunu's own vendored data_2017/shift_data_2.txt is byte-identical (diffed directly) to the compiled-C build's input_data/shift_data_2.txt (the withdrawn slot's own file, same 100-value row), confirming this is genuinely the SAME dead data, not a differently-numbered copy of the real Zakharov vector. Since sezgi's own fid 2 does not exist (Cec2017Error::Withdrawn), and opfunu's F2 does not correspond to any real CEC2017 function at all, this is expected-disagreement-BY-CONSTRUCTION for every point of fid 3 -- per this task's explicit scope ruling, F2 is treated as unconditionally excluded, same root cause class as the general offset bug below but singled out because its target data is not merely wrong, it is DEAD.
divergence_classes.opfunu-unimodal-hybrid-data-source-offse: NEW for CEC2017 (this task's own finding). For every opfunu class F3..F19 (sezgi fid 4..20), the class's OWN `f_shift`/`f_matrix` constructor defaults use `shift_data_<k>` / `M_<k>_D` where `k` is the class's OWN CONTIGUOUS index (e.g. F32017's `f_shift="shift_data_3"`, F42017's `f_shift="shift_data_4"`, grepped directly from opfunu/cec_based/cec2017.py) -- NOT `k+1`, the file the C reference's own gapped func_num numbering actually assigns to that Table-row's formula (e.g. Table row 3 is Rosenbrock, whose REAL C data is shift_data_4.txt/M_4_D<dim>.txt, func_num 4 -- cec17_test_func.cpp's own `case 4: rosenbrock_func(...)`). So opfunu's F3 class computes Rosenbrock's FORMULA on Zakharov's OWN shift/rotation data (func_num 3's real files) -- a formula/data mismatch that does not correspond to ANY function in the real 29-function suite. This recurs identically for every one of F3..F19 (all grepped directly: each uses `shift_data_<own index>`, never `<own index>+1`) -- the SAME root cause as 'opfunu-f2-bogus-withdrawn-data' above (an unapplied +1 gap adjustment), just landing on a REAL (if wrong) function's data instead of the withdrawn slot's dead data. Verified empirically (not merely by source reading): t8_probe_remap.py evaluated every opfunu F1..F29 class against every sezgi fid at 3 independent points (zeros, ones10, a seeded random point, dim=10) with a 1e-6 relative tolerance -- ZERO of F3..F19 matched ANY sezgi fid at all three points simultaneously (this task's report has the full 29-row output transcript).
divergence_classes.opfunu-composition-missing-component-sca: NEW for CEC2017 (this task's own finding, DIFFERENT bug shape from every cec2014_reference_values.json composition class -- those were shift/rotation-matrix misalignments; this is a missing SCALE constant). Unlike F3..F19, opfunu's composition classes F20..F27 (sezgi fid 21-28) DO correctly apply the +1 gap adjustment in their own file selection (F202017's own `f_shift="shift_data_21", f_matrix="M_21_D"` -- the REAL cf01/fid21 data, grepped directly) -- but at least one per-component base-function call inside `evaluate()` omits the component's own `sh_rate` scale constant the C reference's `sr_func` always applies internally. Verified via a targeted diagnostic probe this task (t8_diag_f20.py, dim=10, x=zeros): F202017's own Rastrigin component computes `z2 = np.dot(self.f_matrix[2*ndim:3*ndim,:], x - self.f_shift[2])` -- NO `5.12/100` scale (contrast its own Rosenbrock component two lines above, which DOES apply `2.048/100` correctly) -- giving `g2_raw=23139.686348881736` where an independent from-the-raw-files replica (this task's own script, matching sezgi's own `cb::f4_base` on the CORRECTLY `5.12/100`-scaled `z`) gives `164.075995` -- a ~141x error for that one component alone, which (weighted heavily by `cf_cal`'s own distance-based weighting, since this component's own delta=30 is the largest of the three) dominates F20's own final output: opfunu reports 21205.36 at x=zeros vs the compiled C's (and sezgi's own, cross-validated) 2828.61 -- roughly 7.5x off. Every one of fid 21-28's own composition_spec table (cec2017/mod.rs's module doc) includes at least one nontrivial-`sh_rate` component (Rastrigin 5.12/100, HGBat/HappyCat/Katsuura/GrieRosen 5/100, Schwefel 1000/100, Griewank 600/100, Weierstrass 0.5/100) -- this task verified the bug concretely for fid 21 only (F20) and, given every other fid 22-28 shares the SAME `F202017`-derived `evaluate()` shape (each subclass only overrides `__init__`'s component list, not the scale-application logic itself, per direct reading of F212017..F272017), generalizes the finding rather than re-running the same diagnostic nine more times -- this generalization is flagged here explicitly, not individually re-verified per fid. [Review correction (task-8 review, controller-applied): the 'missing scale' mechanism was verified to hold only for fid 21-24 (opfunu F202017-F232017, which DO index each component's own f_shift[i]; fid 22's Schwefel component additionally lacks the rotation-matrix multiply entirely). For fid 25-28 (F242017-F272017) the reviewer's direct source read found the ACTUAL mechanism is the shared-shift bug: every non-leading component uses self.f_shift[0] instead of its own row -- the same bug class as the opfunu-composition-hybrid-shared-shift tag documents for fid 29-30 (F252017 even keeps the correct line commented out above the buggy one). Runtime-confirmed opfunu-side for fid 25: F242017.evaluate(zeros, dim=10)=4262.29 vs compiled C 4820.81. The exclusion of fid 21-28 from the opfunu comparison is unaffected; only the mechanism attribution for 25-28 is corrected here.]
divergence_classes.opfunu-composition-hybrid-shared-shift: NEW for CEC2017 (this task's own finding, DIFFERENT bug shape again -- a shared-shift copy-paste bug, closer in SHAPE to CEC2022's own 'opfunu-composition-shift-o1' class cec2014_reference_values.json's header references, but independently verified here for this suite, not assumed to recur). opfunu's F28/F29 classes (sezgi fid 29/30, cf09/cf10's hybrid-in-composition) construct their THREE sub-hybrid instances ALL with the SAME `self.f_shift[0]` (component 0's own shift row), quoted VERBATIM from F282017.__init__: `self.g0 = F142017(self.ndim, None, self.f_shift[0], self.f_matrix[:self.ndim,:], self.f_shuffle[0], 0)`, `self.g1 = F152017(self.ndim, None, self.f_shift[0], self.f_matrix[self.ndim:2*self.ndim,:], self.f_shuffle[1], 0)`, `self.g2 = F162017(...,  self.f_shift[0], ...)` -- `g1`/`g2` should each get their OWN component's shift (`self.f_shift[1]`/`self.f_shift[2]`), not component 0's, yet all three literally read index `[0]`. F292017 (fid30) has the IDENTICAL pattern (re-read directly, not assumed): `self.g0/g1/g2` all constructed with `self.f_shift[0]`. This means every sub-hybrid past the first evaluates on the WRONG shift vector (component 0's, not its own), compounding with the general per-component-base-function scale issue above wherever a sub-hybrid's own component list includes a scaled base.
